question: True or false: a typical landlocked country trades about as much as a typical coastal one?
answer: False. Limão and Venables found the median landlocked country trades only about 30% as much as the median coastal economy, and a representative one pays about 50% more to move goods. Every container must cross a neighbour's roads, borders and ports first. Distance to the sea is paid on every single shipment.
move: A cost paid on every transaction outweighs a big cost paid once.
ask: Which small cost do I pay every single day that adds up to more than any big bill?
trap: True, since roads and railways now reach almost everywhere.
source: Limão and Venables, World Bank Economic Review, 2001
reference: Limão & Venables, Infrastructure, Geographical Disadvantage, Transport Costs, and Trade, World Bank Economic Review, 2001
